turns.doctor_question: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been bothering you or what brings you here today?
turns.patient_response: I guess I’m here because the clinic doctor was on me about my eating. I don’t know, I mostly keep it pretty simple—coffee in the morning, maybe a few bites of something between jobs, and then a small dinner if I’m not too busy with class paperwork.

turns.doctor_question: Do you ever find yourself eating a lot in a short period of time, or do you worry a lot about gaining weight?
turns.patient_response: I don’t really do the eating-a-lot-at-once thing. But yeah, I do worry about gaining weight. Like if I eat something heavy, like pizza or a big sandwich, I get this panicky feeling that I’m going to wake up bigger and slower, and then I won’t be able to move around ladders and rooms the way I need to for work.

symptom_reasoning.S049: The patient explicitly denies eating a lot in a short period of time.

turns.doctor_question: Have you ever made yourself sick or used medicine to try to get rid of food after eating, or do you exercise a lot to try to control your weight?
turns.patient_response: I don’t really know. I mean, I don’t think of it that way. I’m on my feet a lot for work anyway, climbing and moving around, so it’s hard to tell what counts as “exercise a lot.” And I don’t really have anything else specific to say about the medicine or making myself sick.

turns.doctor_question: Outside of your regular work activity, do you ever exercise specifically to try to burn off calories or prevent yourself from gaining weight?
turns.patient_response: I’m not really sure. I don’t usually set out to “work out” outside of work. Sometimes I’ll take a walk or keep moving because sitting still makes me feel uneasy, but I don’t have like a gym routine or anything.

symptom_reasoning.S012: The patient reports keeping moving at times because sitting still makes them feel uneasy, suggesting subjective restlessness.

turns.doctor_question: Outside of your work, do you ever restrict what you eat, push yourself to move more, or do anything else specifically to try to keep from gaining weight?
turns.patient_response: Yeah… I guess I do keep what I eat pretty limited. The clinic doctor was kind of getting on me about it, which is why I’m here. Most days it’s just coffee in the morning, maybe a few bites of something between jobs, and then a small dinner if I’m not too busy with class paperwork.

symptom_reasoning.S043: The patient states that they keep their intake "pretty limited" and describes only coffee, a few bites of food, and a small dinner most days.

turns.doctor_question: When you limit what you eat, is it mostly because you're afraid of gaining weight or changing your body shape?
turns.patient_response: Yeah… mostly, I think. If I eat something heavier, like pizza or a big sandwich, I get really anxious that I’m going to wake up bigger somehow, or feel slower. And with my work, moving around ladders and rooms all day, that scares me.

symptom_reasoning.S045: The patient states that eating heavier foods causes anxiety about waking up bigger, indicating fear of weight gain or body-size change.

turns.doctor_question: When you worry about gaining weight, do you see yourself as bigger than you actually are, or feel like even small amounts of food will change your body significantly?
turns.patient_response: Yeah… I think it’s more like I feel even a small or heavier meal will change me right away. Like if I eat pizza or a big sandwich, I get this panicky feeling that I’ll wake up bigger and slower, and then I won’t be able to move around ladders and rooms the way I need to.

symptom_reasoning.S045: The patient reports panic that even a small or heavy meal will rapidly make them bigger, consistent with fear of weight gain.

turns.doctor_question: Does your concern about gaining weight or your body shape cause you to avoid certain foods, situations, or activities, or interfere with your daily routine or responsibilities?
turns.patient_response: Yeah, it does some. I’m still getting to my jobs and going to class, so it’s not like I’ve stopped everything. But I’ve started avoiding lunch with coworkers, or study meetups, because then I have to deal with food being there or people noticing what I’m eating. It just feels easier to keep my routine really tight and not have anyone commenting on it.

symptom_reasoning.S064: The patient reports avoiding lunches with coworkers and study meetups because food is present and others may notice or comment on their eating, indicating avoidance that impairs social routine.

turns.doctor_question: Do you judge yourself mainly based on your weight or body shape?
turns.patient_response: I don’t know if it’s mainly that. I mean, I do think about it, but I’m not sure I’d say my whole opinion of myself is based on my weight or shape. It’s more that I get really uncomfortable and caught up in it sometimes.

turns.doctor_question: Have you ever been told by a doctor or health professional that your weight is too low or that you’re underweight?
turns.patient_response: Not a doctor, no. I mean, people at job sites have said I look too thin, and my work pants are hanging pretty loose now. But I guess I’ve been thinking of it more like I’ve just leaned out from being on my feet all day.

turns.doctor_question: Have you ever lost a significant amount of weight in a short period of time, or do you currently weigh yourself often to track changes in your weight?
turns.patient_response: I haven’t really been tracking it closely on a scale. I just know my work pants are hanging a lot looser, and people on job sites keep saying I look too thin. I’ve kind of been telling myself it’s just from being on my feet all day and getting leaned out.

turns.doctor_question: Have you intentionally tried to lose weight or become thinner, and if so, how much of your weight loss would you say was intentional?
turns.patient_response: I guess some of it has been intentional, yeah. I’ve been keeping my eating pretty limited. I don’t know exactly how much of the weight loss is from that, but the clinic doctor was pretty on me about how little I’ve been eating.

symptom_reasoning.S043: The patient states that they have intentionally kept their eating "pretty limited," describing only coffee, a few bites between jobs, and a small dinner most days.

turns.doctor_question: When you look in the mirror or think about your body, do you feel like you still need to lose more weight even if others say you're already too thin or underweight?
turns.patient_response: Yeah, I guess I don’t see it the way other people do. I don’t look at myself and think it’s some emergency. To me it feels more like everyone’s making a big deal out of it, like I’m just being disciplined and busy. I know they say I look too thin, but it doesn’t really feel that serious to me.

symptom_reasoning.S084: The patient minimizes the seriousness of being described as too thin, characterizing others' concerns as an overreaction to being 'disciplined and busy.'

turns.doctor_question: Has your weight loss happened even though you haven’t been sick, on any medications, or under a doctor’s care for it?
turns.patient_response: I’m not really sure. I mean, I haven’t been under a doctor’s care for losing weight or anything like that. I don’t think I’ve been sick in some obvious way, but I guess I haven’t really looked into it much.

turns.doctor_question: Do you feel like your weight or the way you look is 'wrong' in some way, even if you can't quite explain it?
turns.patient_response: I don’t know if I’d say I feel “wrong,” exactly. I just don’t see it as some emergency the way everyone else seems to. To me it feels like they’re making a big deal out of it, and I’m just trying to stay disciplined and keep up with everything.

symptom_reasoning.S084: The patient minimizes others' concern about their weight and does not view it as an emergency, framing it instead as discipline and busyness.
